medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 5 days

documents.title: Emergency Department Visit Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department - Physician Record
Arrival 03/08/2024 21:10. Faxed to PCP 03/12/2024.

CC: vomiting x 2 days.

HPI: 26-year-old woman with bulimia nervosa and a prior ED visit for dehydration, now vomiting for two days and unable to keep down food or fluids. No diarrhea, fever or travel. States her bulimia has been harder to control over the past few weeks.

PMH: bulimia nervosa (purging), GAD, history of anabolic steroid and loop diuretic misuse, prior dehydration. Meds: fluoxetine 20 mg. NKDA.

VS: BP 95/60, HR 110.
Exam: dry, tired-appearing. Abdomen soft, nontender. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear.

Labs: Na 130, K 2.9, Cl 90, HCO3 32, BUN 28, Cr 0.9. Urine Cl 10. ABG pH 7.50, pCO2 42. Urine hCG negative.

Assessment: Hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis from vomiting, with hypovolemia and hypokalemia. Chloride-responsive (urine Cl 10).

ED course: normal saline with KCl added, IV ondansetron. Tolerated PO by early morning, HR 88, BP 108/66.

Discharge: KCl 20 mEq PO twice daily x 5 days. Follow up with PCP in 3-5 days for repeat electrolytes. Encouraged to reconnect with eating disorder treatment.

Emergency physician

conditions.label: Hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis secondary to vomiting with hypovolemia

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED Fri night: 2 days vomiting, K 2.9, HCO3 32, Cl 90, Na 130, urine Cl 10 - contraction/vomiting alkalosis. Fluids + KCl, home on KCl 20 BID x5d (day 5 today).

She's candid: purging much more since February, several times a day at the worst, around a stretch of long hours. Better since Sunday. Not using diuretics or laxatives. Fluoxetine - missed a lot of doses last month.

Vitals ok today, no orthostatic symptoms. Mucous membranes moist. No parotid swelling.

A/P:
1. Hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis with hypovolemia - resolved clinically; BMP and Mg today to confirm. Finish KCl.
2. Bulimia, purging type - relapse. She will call the eating disorder program to restart therapy; I asked her to message me once she has an appointment.
3. GAD - back to daily fluoxetine 20.
RTC ~3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium, chloride and bicarbonate are all back to normal, magnesium normal. You can stop the potassium after today's dose.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thank you. I have a therapy appt on the 21st.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from her office (closed door), consents.
Back in therapy every other week since March. Purging down to occasional. Fluoxetine daily. Home scale steady to up a little. No dizziness. GAD-7 10, PHQ-9 5.
A/P: bulimia improving with therapy back in place; GAD stable on fluoxetine 20. In-person for physical in the fall with labs.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2024-25 flu and COVID given, one in each arm. No contraindications. Pt left after 15 min, no issues.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 26 (27 in a couple of weeks).
Interval: good stretch since the spring. Therapy every 2-3 weeks. Purging rare by her account. No diuretics, laxatives, steroids. Fluoxetine daily. Running casually, eats before. Periods regular.
PHQ-9 4, GAD-7 8.
Exam: 51 kg - best weight since I've known her post-2021. Vitals normal. No parotid enlargement. Heart, lungs, abdomen, skin normal.
A/P:
- Bulimia, purging type: in a better phase, keep the therapy.
- GAD: fluoxetine 20.
- CMP, CBC, Mg, Phos.
- Flu + COVID done 10/8. Pap due next year.
RTC 6 months or prn.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal this year. Keep doing what you're doing.

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So... positive pregnancy test this morning. Two of them actually. Last period started Jan 17. I stopped the fluoxetine over the weekend because I wasn't sure it was safe. I bought prenatal vitamins. What do I do next?

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Congratulations, Taylor. That puts you at about 5 1/2 weeks, due date around October 24. Next step is an OB - I've placed a referral and they'll call you for a first prenatal visit. Keep the prenatal vitamin going.

On fluoxetine: it is one of the better-studied antidepressants in pregnancy, and stopping can bring the anxiety and the eating symptoms back. It's your decision, and it's one to make with OB too - I'd rather you not make it alone. Please also tell your OB about the eating disorder so they can watch weight and labs closely. Message me any time.

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. I think I'll stay off it for now and talk to the OB.

documents.title: Antepartum Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Antepartum unit - Discharge Summary
Admitted 03/15/2025, discharged 03/18/2025. Received 04/29/2025.

Patient: 27-year-old G1 at 8w1d by LMP (01/17/2025).

Reason for admission: three weeks of severe nausea and vomiting, 4-5 episodes a day, with difficulty keeping down food and fluids and a 6 kg weight loss since onset. Background of bulimia nervosa (purging type) and a previous ED visit for vomiting-related metabolic alkalosis.

Admission findings: BP 100/60, HR 98. Appeared dehydrated. Weight 45 kg.
Na 135, K 3.0, Cl 90, HCO3 32; blood gas pH 7.50, PaCO2 45; urine chloride 15.

Diagnosis: Hyperemesis gravidarum with hypokalemic, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis.

Hospital course: IV crystalloid with potassium replacement, IV thiamine before dextrose, scheduled IV antiemetics. Advanced to oral intake on day 2, oral potassium on day 3. Tolerating meals and fluids at discharge. Discussed overlap with her eating disorder history; she reports no intentional purging during this pregnancy.

Discharge medications:
- doxylamine-pyridoxine 10 mg/10 mg DR, 2 tablets at bedtime
- ondansetron 4 mg ODT every 8 hours as needed
- prenatal vitamin daily
Home fluoxetine listed; patient states she stopped it in February.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: OB clinic in 1 week; return for inability to keep fluids down.

Obstetrics hospitalist

documents.title: Pt reports hospital stay
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Was admitted Sat-Tues for severe vomiting in pregnancy ("hyperemesis"), got IV fluids and potassium. Home on two nausea meds from OB. Keeping liquids and small meals down. No discharge paperwork sent to us - pt will ask OB. Scheduled with PCP next week.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
9w4d. Admitted 3/15-3/18 to the antepartum unit for hyperemesis (no summary yet; history from pt). Had her first OB visit at the start of March, so the referral is complete.

Now: nausea most of the day but vomiting once or twice, keeping fluids and small meals down with the doxylamine-pyridoxine at night and ondansetron as needed. Prenatal vitamin daily, takes it at night with a snack. Off fluoxetine since February; anxiety up some (GAD-7 12) - mostly about the pregnancy. She is clear the vomiting is not self-induced. I believe her, and told her I'd rather she tell me if that changes than hide it.

Exam: 46 kg (45 at admission, by her report). Vitals fine. Mucous membranes moist.

A/P:
1. Hyperemesis gravidarum - improving on OB regimen. BMP today. Per OB: call for inability to keep fluids down.
2. Pregnancy 9w4d - OB managing. Added OB meds and prenatal vitamin to our list.
3. GAD / bulimia - off fluoxetine by choice; revisit with OB if anxiety climbs. Suggested she let her therapist know about the pregnancy.
RTC 2-3 months or as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your potassium and the rest of the chemistry are back to normal. Good sign that the regimen is working.

documents.title: Obstetric Triage Note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Obstetric Triage - provider note, 05/10/2025 (copy received 06/17/2025)

27 y/o G1 at 16w1d, known hyperemesis gravidarum (antepartum admission two months ago), bulimia nervosa (purging type) and prior laxative/diuretic misuse. Reports vomiting about ten times a day for the past two weeks, can't hold down food or liquids, weak and lightheaded. Down 4 kg (9 lb) over those two weeks. Prenatal course has otherwise been uncomplicated. Tearful, asks why she is the one friend who is pregnant and sick all the time.

Current meds: prenatal vitamin only (has run out of / stopped her antiemetics, per patient). Fluoxetine on old list, not taking. NKDA.

VS: P 112, BP 94/56. Wt 44.5 kg.
Exam: fatigued, mucous membranes dry. Abdomen soft, nontender, uterus appropriate for dates.
Urine dip: ketones moderate.
Bedside US: single intrauterine pregnancy, viable, cardiac activity present.

A/P: Hyperemesis gravidarum, recurrent, with dehydration and ketonuria.
- 2 L IV fluids, IV ondansetron.
- Observed overnight; tolerating clear liquids and crackers this morning, HR 86.
- Discharge on doxylamine-pyridoxine 2 tabs QHS and ondansetron ODT q8h PRN (new supply sent). Prenatal vitamin.
- OB clinic within the week. Return for inability to keep fluids down.

OB triage provider

documents.title: Back in triage
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I was back at L&D triage over the weekend, throwing up constantly again. They gave me fluids overnight and restarted the nausea meds. I had stopped them because I thought I was past it. Feeling better today. OB appt Thursday.

documents.title: RE: Back in triage
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm sorry - that sounds miserable. Please keep taking both meds until OB says otherwise. Can we see you in a few weeks to check weight and how you're doing overall?

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20w4d. Triage 5/10 for recurrent hyperemesis (fluids overnight) - triage note not received; pt summary. Since restarting both antiemetics: vomiting "maybe every other day," eating small frequent meals.
Anxiety moderate, GAD-7 10. Still off fluoxetine; seeing her therapist monthly. No purging.
Wt 47.5 kg, up 3 kg since triage. Vitals normal.
A/P: hyperemesis improving; pregnancy per OB; GAD/bulimia stable off meds. Flu shot in the fall here. RTC after delivery, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Records filed

documents.body: OB triage note from 5/10/25 received by fax and scanned. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 36w4d. Inactivated flu vaccine IM L deltoid (recommended in pregnancy). No egg or vaccine reactions. Tolerated well. Pt says she had Tdap at OB in August.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Labor and Delivery - Discharge Summary
Admitted 10/20/2025, discharged 10/22/2025. Copy received 12/02/2025.

27 y/o G1 at 39w3d, admitted in spontaneous labor.
Pregnancy notable for hyperemesis gravidarum (admission at 8 weeks, triage visit at 16 weeks), resolving in the second trimester. History of bulimia nervosa and GAD; off fluoxetine during pregnancy. Prenatal labs unremarkable. Tdap given 08/12/2025.

Delivery 10/20/2025: uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery. Healthy infant.
Postpartum course routine. Afebrile, vitals normal, ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet.

Discharge meds: prenatal vitamin. Antiemetics no longer needed.
Follow-up: postpartum visit with OB at 6 weeks. PCP follow-up for anxiety/eating disorder care.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Baby is here

documents.body: Delivered on the 20th, everything went smoothly and the baby is healthy. Exhausted but good. Wanted to let you know. I'll book a visit once things settle.

documents.title: RE: Baby is here
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! So happy for you. Rest when you can. Let's see you in about 6 weeks - and reach out sooner if your mood or eating start to slide.

documents.title: Postpartum Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
7 weeks postpartum, SVD 10/20 at term, healthy baby (came with her today, sleeping in the car seat). L&D discharge summary arrived last week - uncomplicated. Saw OB for the 6-week check.

Mood: tired, but no persistent low mood, no intrusive thoughts. Anxiety creeping up in the first weeks home, so she restarted her fluoxetine 20 mg on her own about 3 weeks after delivery - taking it daily. Eating: "structured, I'm trying." Denies purging, laxatives, diuretics. Restarting therapy in January.
PHQ-9 7, GAD-7 9.

Exam: 53 kg. Vitals normal. Well appearing, appropriate.

A/P:
1. Postpartum - pregnancy and hyperemesis resolved. Stopped doxylamine-pyridoxine and ondansetron on the list.
2. GAD - back on fluoxetine 20 mg daily (it never came off our list). Good plan.
3. Bulimia - watchful; restarting therapy. Asked her to message me if purging returns.
4. Tdap 8/12/25 at OB per discharge summary - added to immunization record.
RTC 3 months.
